newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid air cargo volume up 10.5 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Madrid air cargo volume up 10.5 pct in May.

text.p: Cargo traffic at Madrid's Barajas airport rose 10.5 percent to 21,818 tonnes in May as strong scheduled traffic made up for a fall in charter cargo, the airport authority said.

Domestic and international traffic increased at equal rates while scheduled freight business grew 15.8 percent in the month and charter business fell 38.2 percent to account for only 1,198 tonnes of the total.
Barajas handled 110,657 tonnes of cargo in the first five months of this year, 11.4 percent more than the same period 1996.
Domestic freight has risen 15.8 percent in the year to date to 34,628 tonnes while international cargo is 9.5 percent ahead of last year at 76,029 tonnes.

Passenger numbers rose 6.8 percent in May to 1.95 million, or 9.31 million in the five month period, an increase of 10.8 percent. The number of air transport movements increased 3.5 percent to 21,920 in the month, taking the accumulated total to 106,556.
